newsitem.title: FRANCE: Congo rebels row back on French bomb threat.
newsitem.headline: Congo rebels row back on French bomb threat.

text.p: A spokesman for the new Democratic Republic of Congo's rulers rowed back on Tuesday on a threat to plant bombs in France if Paris gave shelter to ousted Zaire president Mobutu Sese Seko, attributing it to over-exuberence.
An embarrassed N'Zamba Afri-Ku-Nyeng said he had made the bomb threat in the heat of excitement at the victory of Laurent Kabila's rebels and the French government was not amused.
"My words exceeded my thoughts. Why should we put bombs now that we have won if we did nothing against France during the struggle?" he asked.
Talking to reporters outside the Zairean embassy in Paris on Sunday after police prevented him and supporters from taking over the building, Afri-Ku-Nyeng had threatened to "plant bombs in France".
He said police had later called at his home in an emergency investigation ordered by the capital's police chief.
"I would not be surprised to hear that they want to expel me," he said. He said he had been living in France for 20 years and his residence permit was valid until 2004.

"The possibility that Mobutu may come to France is not of our concern. It concerns French sovereignty," he later said in a statement in his capacity as as president of the Coordination of the Committees of Vigilance and Support to the rebels.
Afri-Ku-Nyeng said he believed Mobutu may go into exile in Brazil, as he had reports that a residence he owns in Rio de Janeiro was being painted anew.
French Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said Mobutu had not made any request to come to France.
"I suppose he has a permanent entry visa," he added.
Mobutu, who was in Togo's capital Lome on Tuesday, made several stays over the past few months in a villa he owns on the French Riviera and a flat in Paris.
Morocco has said it was prepared to give him asylum.
Afri-Ku-Nyeng also toned down his threat to hunt down Mobutu wherever he goes in exile. "Mobutu has been dethroned. We rather pity him," he said.
But he said in his communique: "We nevertheless believe that the ex-dictator of the ex-Zaire must be detained and brought to trial for crimes against humanity".
Rebel chief Laurent Kabila has changed Zaire's name to the Democratic Republic of Congo and proclaimed himself head of state.

Afri-Ku-Nyeng also said the new government wanted to recover the Mobutu family's property in France which he said included Mobutu's palatial Riviera villa at Roquebrune Cap Martin, a huge flat on Paris most expensive Avenue Foch, three flats owned by Mobutu's daughter in the posh Paris suburb of Neuilly.
Rummelhardt said France had not received any request to freeze Mobutu's assets.

The French daily Le Monde, quoting Belgian banking sources, said Mobutu had over the past few years transferred to South Africa most of his assets in Switzerland, which froze his assets last week, and Belgium.
Afri-Ku-Nyeng said Mobutu also had large assets in Brunei and bank accounts in the Mediterranean principality of Monaco.
